Real Madrid's Kylian Mbappe scores his team's third goal [Jose Jordan/AFP]By AFPPublished On 7 Nov 20267 Nov 2026
Kylian Mbappe scored for the seventh match running as Real Madrid pulled provisionally level on points with La Liga leaders Barcelona after a 3-0 win at 10-man Valencia.
Reigning champions Barca visit Atletico Madrid, third, on Sunday, aiming to move back clear of the chasing pack.
Jose Mourinho’s Madrid largely dominated at Mestalla Stadium on Saturday, securing an eighth win in a row across all competitions.
Federico Valverde and Arda Guler’s first-half goals put Madrid in the driving seat, and Mbappe added a third in the second half.
Los Blancos were without winger Vinicius Junior, who was serving the final game of a four-match ban.
Madrid have thrived in his absence, putting heavy pressure on Barca, whom they beat in the Camp Nou Clasico on October 25.
In the ninth minute, the match stopped for players and fans to pay tribute to Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel, who tragically died on Tuesday.
Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois made a smart save to deny Aaron Mayol, who had picked Aurelien Tchouameni’s pocket in a dangerous area.
Valencia’s Guido Rodriguez had a goal disallowed for offside before Mourinho’s side took control.
Valverde drilled Madrid ahead from outside the area after Mbappe’s free kick was blocked by the Valencia wall and fell to the Uruguayan.
Guler soon doubled the lead after Jude Bellingham’s cross was deflected kindly into his path.
Guler had a good chance for the third early in the second half, but Valencia goalkeeper Stole Dimitrievski grabbed the ball as the midfielder tried to round him. Advertisement

Italy says civilian infrastructure in Europe is “under attack”.
A series of bomb threats this week grounded flights and put airports on high alert. No explosives were found, and the threats appear to be false.

Former Israeli military chief Gadi Eisenkot is the leader of the Yashar party [File: Shir Torem/Reuters]By Al Jazeera StaffPublished On 7 Nov 20267 Nov 2026
Israel’s President Isaac Herzog has tasked Gadi Eisenkot with forming the country’s next government, passing over the former army chief’s rival, Benjamin Netanyahu.
Herzog told Eisenkot of his decision on Saturday evening and will formally hand him the mandate at a ceremony on Sunday, the president’s spokesperson said.
Recommended Stories list of 3 itemslist 1 of 3Jerusalem Daily: Arab parties back Eisenkot against Netanyahulist 2 of 3Palestinian citizens of Israel put to ‘loyalty test’ after election winslist 3 of 3President Herzog faces key choice as Israel struggles to form governmentend of list
Herzog held consultations with political parties this week to decide who he would appoint to form a government after neither side secured a majority in the October 27 general election.
Some 67 lawmakers, including from Arab-led parties, endorsed Eisenkot, leader of the Yashar party, to form the next government, while only 46 backed Netanyahu, the current prime minister.
Eisenkot will have 28 days – with a possible 14-day extension – to build a coalition of at least 61 of the Knesset’s 120 seats, the minimum threshold for a government.
In the October election, Eisenkot’s four-party alliance won 48 seats, while Netanyahu’s right-wing and religious bloc secured 53, leaving both short of the 61 needed for a parliamentary majority. Arab-led parties, representing Palestinian citizens of Israel, won a record 19 seats.

People protest against the cost of living and rising fuel prices in Paris, France, November 7, 2026 [Stephanie Lecocq/Reuters]By Al Jazeera Staff and AFPPublished On 7 Nov 20267 Nov 2026
Tens of thousands of people have protested across France for a fourth consecutive weekend, in another show of anger against the government.
About 146,000 people rallied across the country to protest against the rising cost of living on Saturday, including 46,000 in Paris, the Ministry of the Interior said.
Recommended Stories list of 3 itemslist 1 of 3Photos: Thousands rally in France over rising costs and economic struggleslist 2 of 3Mass protests in France driven by nationwide strike actionlist 3 of 3Radical or hero?: France debates leftist candidate Jean-Luc Melenchonend of list
Unions put the figure at 250,000 protesters nationwide, with 75,000 in the capital.
The demonstrations come just days after an estimated 575,000 people took part in a rally organised by trade unions.
About 70,000 security personnel were deployed across the country on Saturday, with Interior Minister Laurent Nunez warning that authorities would be “ready and waiting” for anyone engaging in rioting or looting.
Clashes broke out between police and some protesters in the capital, Paris, despite a lower turnout than in previous weeks.
Footage posted online by the CLPRESS news agency showed police charging at protesters and using tear gas in an attempt to disperse the crowds. A police officer was also seen hitting a protester with a baton.
Police said a group of 200 individuals attacked officers as they were arresting a man who had set fire to a rubbish bin in a square in Paris, the AFP news agency reported.
